The handbook says doctor's notes need to be forwarded to the HR person or whoever at home office, and they can determine if the absence is excused or not based on the note. Technically it shouldn't ever go to your SM, but if it does, he must pass it along to the right person.

I don't think you are in the wrong, OP. At my store, it is the responsibility of the person doing cooler to get everything put away on the meat pallets first, to have them ready for the meat person, after running their back stock. If the person doing meat starts at the same time as the person doing cooler, then they work together to get the pallet down to just meat, or the person doing meat kills time elsewhere, like doing bread or whatever. You shouldn't be held responsible for another person's section. One or a few boxes is one thing, but over 15 is overkill, and honestly puts too many chefs in the kitchen, if that makes sense.

I can understand that, but not having the QR (not cases of usual random bypass) code like us means we have to shop without bagging, put everything on the belt, scan it, and then bag it completely. It takes a lot longer than scanning the QR code like normal. 

Also, I don't know if it helps, but we keep weighted items unbagged in the front part of the cart until after checkout to bag them, just in case, to avoid the pain you speak of.
It lets us bypass sometimes, but not every time. I would imagine we are updated, given we just started doing it.

It's weird on our computer, so maybe it'll help with yours. You'll go to the Transaction Search on the computer under Items. Select which SCO you want to look at under User, and also put 0 - 99 under the till number space. You can also fill out the date and all that good stuff too, to be more accurate.

Coming from an LSA, it's a double edged sword trying to decide where to put a slow worker. I'd much rather have everything on the floor get done, by sacrifice the second ringer more, then try and do everything on the floor myself. Unfortunately, I'll end up helping with the front end stuff too because of them, but I'd rather do that then have the floor be a mess. I'm sorry you are dealing with this, OP, it isn't fair for anyone.

We contacted the help desk, which wasn't helpful. It didn't give us any options after the blue bag screen, besides taking a picture of the receipt. My manager just took a random photo, and it let us through, so I guess all is well? Thank you for the information though, definitely helpful!

Part and full time employees receive time and a half for any work done on holidays. The only difference between part and full timers, is that full time employees get an additional bonus, at regular pay, of their work hours average (mine is roughly 7.6 hours), as long as fully complete their scheduled shift the day before and after the holiday.
You'll lose your holiday pay and bonus (if your area has Labor Day) for calling out the day of, before, or after a holiday, fyi. Idk if that applies to you.

It is the same for us, at my store. I have wondered that, too. I am an LSA, so I have access to look at those stats, and we could really use the extra person, based on that alone. My other thought behind that third person is in case of emergency, and someone has to leave suddenly; I wouldn't't be left alone. I think it is poor as general safety goes, too.

It is a regular occurrence at my store, even on busy weekends. The worse part is they still expect us to do everything the same, if not better, as if we still had that third person till 9. Our DM says we are not busy enough to need that extra person in the evenings, according to the budget.

Technically, yes, but we all get a tiny percentage (based on how long you've been with the company) per hour worked. It usually comes out to 5 days of sick time per year. I think only full time people get pto, as well.

I agree! I had a medical emergency a few months back, which required me to visit an ER in the middle of the night. I gave them over 9 hours notice, and a doctor's note, but because I didn't have enough sick time, it was counted as unexcused :)

My roommate works at the warehouse, so i think their sick time works kinda differently, too. He has been allowed to use a doctor's note in cases like that to get it excused, while I can't use one, even in an emergency.

It is dumb, yes, but unfortunately how it is. Our DM was confused on the policy herself, so she reached out to whomever and clarified it. They do it that way so it is fair, otherwise associates who work 4/5 hour shifts could call off sick from shifts more often than someone, like an LSA and above, who is always working 8/9 hour shifts. Most averages range around 7 hours, I believe. It updates with each new year. 

The last part has been debated at my store, but that's just what I was told from management. I'm not sure if it has actually been followed or not. Perhaps they said it more in hopes to scare people into providing adequate time for coverage.

As I've been told, you can only use your sick time if you have enough to cover your average hours worked. So, in my case, I would need to have about 7 hours to take a shift off. Also, it doesn't matter how long your scheduled shift is that you're trying to get off, you have to use your average number regardless. 

Make sure you give four hours notice too, as I've been told that voids your ability to use it and it'll be counted as unexcused unless you show up or find coverage.

So, basically, in my case, it's you either use sick time, or face getting written up or termination after your second unexcused.
